    Read many square fields, for example cell galleries

    Source: R/image-windows.R
    sg_read_fields.Rd

    Reads one sg_read_field() per row of a table of centres. Each row names its image through source, looked up in paths.

    Usage

    sg_read_fields(
  centres,
  paths,
  channels = character(0),
  size,
  pixel_size = 1,
  fill = 0,
  x = "x",
  y = "y",
  source = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  channel_columns = NULL,
  key_prefix = ""
)

    Arguments

    centres

    Data frame with centre coordinates and the image key.

    paths

    Named character vector or list: image key to file path, or a single path used for all rows when source is NULL.

    channels

    Channel names or numbers read for every field.

    size, pixel_size, fill

    As in sg_read_field().

    x, y, source

    Column names of the centre coordinates and image key.

    id

    Optional column used to name the fields.

    channel_columns

    Optional columns of centres naming further channels to read for each row (for example a row-specific marker).

    key_prefix

    Prefix added to the source values before looking them up in paths.

    Value

    A named list of sg_field objects in row order; each carries the table row (as a one-row data frame) in row.

    See also

    sg_read_field()

    Examples

    f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
planes <- list(matrix(1:100, 10, 10), matrix(101:200, 10, 10))
invisible(tiff::writeTIFF(lapply(planes, function(p) p / 255), f,
                          bits.per.sample = 8L))
cells <- data.frame(id = c("a", "b"), x = c(2.5, 4), y = c(2.5, 3))
fields <- sg_read_fields(cells, f, channels = c("ch1", "ch2"), size = 2,
                         pixel_size = 0.5, id = "id")
fields$b$channels$ch2
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]  165  175  185  195
#> [2,]  166  176  186  196
#> [3,]  167  177  187  197
#> [4,]  168  178  188  198
